name: express-map
description: Visual route, middleware, and template navigation for Express apps

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Express Map performs static analysis only and never executes user code.

enumDescriptions: Underline in the editor only, without adding an entry to the Problems panel.
expressMap.diagnostics.brokenTemplateRef.markdownDescription:
Severity for `res.render('name')` calls naming a template that isn't in the views directory.

Turn this down for apps that register view directories at runtime, or render templates produced by a build step, where the file is genuinely absent from the source tree and genuinely present when the app runs.

The **Broken References** section of the tree is unaffected by this setting.

enumDescriptions: Underline in the editor only, without adding an entry to the Problems panel.
expressMap.diagnostics.asyncErrorHandlin.markdownDescription:
Severity for async route handlers with no `try`/`catch`.

This is already suppressed automatically for projects where the framework catches rejected promises — Express 5, or `express-async-errors` / `express-async-handler` in the dependency list — and for handlers wrapped in a helper such as `asyncHandler(...)`. Use this if your error handling takes a form Express Map can't see.

The **Potential Issues** section of the tree is unaffected by this setting.

expressMap.excludeDirs.markdownDescription:
Additional directory names to skip when scanning the views directory for template files — for example `["dist", "build", "coverage"]`.

These are directory *names*, not glob patterns: a name listed here is skipped wherever it appears in the walk. `node_modules`, `.git` and `out` are always skipped and don't need listing.

Useful when a build step copies compiled templates into the views tree, which would otherwise show up as duplicate or orphaned templates.

languageModelTools.name: express-map_analyzeApp
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Returns a structured summary of the Express.js application in the current workspace: all routes (method, path, file, line, template rendered, async flag, error handling), templates, broken template references (res.render calls pointing to missing files), async handlers without try/catch, duplicate routes, orphaned templates never referenced by any route, and global middleware. Use this when the user asks about their Express app's routing structure, API endpoints, template usage, or potential issues.

scripts.pretest: npm run compile && npm run lint
